title: 9/11 Memorial & Museum Launches $75M 'Never Forget Fund' Ahead of 25th Anniversary
detail: The National September 11 Memorial & Museum launched the 'Never Forget Fund,' a $75 million fundraising campaign aimed at educating the roughly 100 million Americans — about a third of the U.S. population — who were not yet born or too young to remember the September 11, 2001 attacks. The campaign, announced with a new public service announcement, had already secured the first $25 million in gifts; former NYC Mayor and Memorial & Museum Chairman Michael Bloomberg pledged through Bloomberg Philanthropies to match the next $25 million raised. Funds will keep museum admission free for students, first responders, and veterans, expand classroom lesson plans and summer teacher institutes, and produce a new 30-minute film of firsthand survivor accounts annually. Chief Advancement and Communications Officer Josh Cherwin said the PSA would 'help build awareness of the approaching anniversary, as well as the programs and mission of the 9/11 Memorial and Museum.' The nonprofit has hosted nearly 97 million memorial visitors and 28 million museum visitors since the museum opened in 2014.
